reason: Design review completed for the four public cases. B1/B2 prototype cases carry strong exact-state assertions, and the two not_applicable documentation cases carry reviewed rationale. Two coverage gaps require repair: the anonymization negative check in public-evidence is defeated by the most plausible wrong result (partial-name leakage), and the requested question-count ceiling is never asserted in public-experiment. Design review only; no execution was performed or claimed.

findings.reason: The anonymization counterexample ('Repeating a supplied participant name') is enforced only by prohibited text_contains 'Dana Sample' on turn 1. The most plausible wrong result is a partial identifier ('Dana praised the idea', 'D. Sample', or the name echoed inside the questions string), which passes every current assertion, and turn 2's json_equals ledger contains no name-bearing field at all. Add observable prohibitions covering each supplied name token individually across both turns (and any supplied email/phone token in future variants), so the assertion distinguishes true anonymization from surname-only stripping.

Both turn-1 inputs request a questions string with '1-5 questions', and the prototype sets a hard ceiling (one block of at most three; product limit five including prose requests), but the only assertion is text_contains '?', which is satisfied by a single question and equally by a ten-question lecture. The stated boundary is unexercised in either direction. Add an observable upper-bound assertion on question count on the questions field (at most five, block at most three) so the bounded question block is distinguished from over-questioning, paired with the existing 'Deferring the experiment behind background questions' counterexample.
